identity.title: Biopharmaceutics and Pharmacokinetics
identity.subtitle: PT-312 Theoretical Notes

authors.name: Staff Members of the Pharmaceutical Technology Department
authors.credit_line: Prepared by the Staff Members of the Pharmaceutical Technology Department

identity.credit_policy: Departmental credit exactly as printed on the source title page; no individual names are added or invented.
identity.rework_authorised_note: No written authorisation from the department is on file; the user commissioned the rework and confirmed the departmental credit line at intake.

figures.notes: Concentration-time curves, semilog plots, compartment schematics and dissolution profiles are redrawn as SVG sources in rework/figures; the source PDF's raster figures are not reused.

audience.prior_knowledge: Physical pharmacy, pharmaceutics and basic calculus (logarithms, exponentials, slopes); no prior pharmacokinetics assumed.
audience.display_line: For pharmacy students taking PT-312 Biopharmaceutics and Pharmacokinetics

goal.notes: Simplify and organise only: same scientific content as the source notes, explained more clearly and laid out as a textbook. No new topics are introduced; worked examples are kept and expanded step by step, and end-of-chapter questions are added as study support.

language.terminology: Keep the standard pharmacokinetic symbols used in the source (Cp, Cp0, AUC, Ke, Ka, t1/2, Vd, CL, MRT, F) and define each on first use.

size.restructuring_note: The 14 subjects of the source contents page become the 14 chapters, in the printed order.

mcq.format: Four-option stems tagged to a learning objective; answers with worked rationales at the end of each chapter.

references.style_note: Numbered square-bracket citations in the text; a single consolidated reference list at the end of the book, as in the source.

must_keep: Departmental credit line and the PT-312 course code
The 14 subjects and their printed order
Every worked example in the source
must_not_change: No invented ISBN, publisher or copyright registration
No new topics beyond the source syllabus
